body:
:+1:

Getting same issue. I tried both with and without the new ignore permissions option. Both on ubuntu 12.04 64bit and 14.04 64bit. On windows is just complains invalid argument but doesn't do anything. On windows I've only had ignore permissions enabled.  None of the systems have synced yet (wanted them all to index themselves and verify things are mostly in sync before activating it.)

That's... bizarre. What does `ls -ld /mnt/Storage/Files/AndroidSync` and `mount | grep Storage` say?

Edit: and `df /mnt/Storage/Files/AndroidSync`
Same here. directories would be set to 40000

I fixed permissions again and waiting for rescan to finish, but since I do have more restricted mount settings:

``` bash
# rikku (Ubuntu 12.04 x64)
/dev/mapper/vg0-srv_homesync on /srv/homesync type ext4 (rw,nodev,relatime)

# nas01 (Ubuntu 14.04 x64)
/dev/mapper/nfsvg0-nfs01 on /srv/nfs01 type ext4 (rw,nodev,noatime)
```
@vrillusions Can you post the above commands for your repository root? Apart from `mount`?
I change the permissions more than one time back. But syncthing also set them back to 000.
Can someone of you who see this problem post the commands above so we can possibly start to narrow down what the problem is?

Ahh so I'm able to narrow it down to just directories.. which I realized @jedie mentioned above. Anyway files in the repository have permissions set fine, it's just the directories.  Interestingly I copied a single folder out so I didn't have to wait for rescan of everything and I can't reproduce the error.

At any rate, the repository root that's having the issue. This is after fixing the permissions again. Don't know if I'll still be awake to provide post-scan values since it takes about an hour to scan it:

``` bash
root@nas01:/srv/nfs01/media# ls -ld /srv/nfs01/media/music
drwxrws--- 8 syncthing users 4096 May 26 00:29 /srv/nfs01/media/music
root@nas01:/srv/nfs01/media# mount | grep nfs01
/dev/mapper/nfsvg0-nfs01 on /srv/nfs01 type ext4 (rw,nodev,noatime)
```
@vrillusions So the user syncthing owns the repo root, and I guess syncthing runs as that user? How does an `ls -la` of that repo root look? (pre/post scan, doesn't matter)

Yep, that's correct. it runs as syncthing and I also added that user to the `users` group

``` bash
root@nas01:/srv/nfs01/media# ls -la /srv/nfs01/media/music
total 480464
drwxrws---  8 syncthing users      4096 May 26 00:29 .
drwxrwsr-x  8 vr        users      4096 May 26 03:31 ..
drwxrws---  3 syncthing users      4096 Apr 19 10:51 downloaded
drwxrws--- 18 syncthing users      4096 May 14 22:09 flac
drwxrws--- 11 syncthing users      4096 May 19 06:44 iTunes
drwxrws---  3 syncthing users      4096 Apr 19 10:51 _my music
drwxrws---  6 syncthing users      4096 Apr 19 10:51 purchased_music
-rw-rw----  1 syncthing users        16 May 26 00:29 .stignore
drwxrws---  4 syncthing users      4096 May  2 18:56 SyncArchive-Old
-rw-rw----  1 syncthing users 491956140 Jun  7  2012 Ultimae - - Random Friday.zip
```

The `.stignore` file has a single line: `SyncArchive-Old`.

(edit)
And those permissions are the same on all files in the folder. namely because to reset things I run:

``` bash
cd /srv/nfs01/media/music
find . -type d -exec chmod 2770 {} \;
find . -type f -exec chmod 660 {} \;
chown -R syncthing:users ./*
```
(for the record, I'm unable to reproduce this with my tests under Ubuntu, hence why I'm fishing for any info about what is different in your setup than mine)

Indeed it's not always happening. I created a `/svr/nfs01/media/synctest` with a single folder from music and that appeared to scan fine. But then the default sync at `/home/syncthing/Sync` is showing the behavior... at any rate I'm heading to bed as its' 4:00 am here but I'll update in the morning.

I have synced with a windows machine:

```
syncthing@lmde-vm ~/test $ ls -la
insgesamt 12
drwx--S---  3 syncthing users 4096 Mai 26 10:06 .
drwsrws--- 16 syncthing users 4096 Mai 26 10:05 ..
drwxrws---  2 syncthing users 4096 Mai 26 10:06 test01
syncthing@lmde-vm ~/test $ mkdir creates_from_linux
...wait after sync...
syncthing@lmde-vm ~/test $ ls -la
insgesamt 20
drwx--S---  5 syncthing users 4096 Mai 26 10:19 .
drwsrws--- 16 syncthing users 4096 Mai 26 10:05 ..
d---------  2 syncthing users 4096 Mai 26 10:17 created_under_windows
d---------  2 syncthing users 4096 Mai 26 10:18 creates_from_linux
d---------  2 syncthing users 4096 Mai 26 10:17 test01
syncthing@lmde-vm ~/test $ 
```
Yes, a small test instance would be good. But how to make? -> http://discourse.syncthing.net/t/how-to-setup-a-small-test-environment/272
I posted an answer there. But according to the original bug report, no syncing is necessary here, just pointing syncthing at a directory and letting it scan.
OK, I've managed to reproduce this when syncthing Linux<->Windows.

I don't see how that should affect the original issue (no Windows there, right?) but it would we nice if you could retest anyway;

https://nym.se/t/syncthing-linux-amd64-v0.8.10-2-g8e05208.tar.gz
